TextView.android:text: Intermediate Lesson 12: Circles and Cyclic Quadrilaterals

The circle is nature's most perfect shape, and its angles possess magical properties:
• Central Angle: An angle formed by two radii. Its measure equals the intercepted arc.
• Inscribed Angle: An angle formed by two chords meeting on the circle. Its measure is exactly HALF of the intercepted arc.
• Thales's Theorem: An inscribed angle that intercepts a diameter (semicircle) is ALWAYS a right angle (90 degrees).
• Alternate Segment Theorem: The angle between a tangent and a chord through the point of contact equals the inscribed angle in the alternate segment.

A cyclic quadrilateral is a four-sided polygon where all four vertices lie on a single circle. These are the holy grail of Olympiad geometry.
Key Properties:
1. Opposite angles sum to 180 degrees (they are supplementary).
2. An exterior angle is equal to the opposite interior angle.
3. Angles subtended by the same arc (or chord) from the same side are equal. If you can prove two angles looking at the same segment are equal, the 4 points are concyclic!

Ptolemy's Theorem is a powerful equation that applies ONLY to cyclic quadrilaterals. 
If a quadrilateral ABCD is inscribed in a circle, then the product of its diagonals equals the sum of the products of its opposite sides.
Formula: AC * BD = (AB * CD) + (BC * AD).
If you have a quadrilateral and this equation holds true, it is guaranteed to be cyclic.

The Power of a Point defines the relationship between lines intersecting a circle.
• Intersecting Chords (Inside): If chords AB and CD intersect at point P, then PA * PB = PC * PD.
• Secants (Outside): If secants from external point P cut the circle at A,B and C,D, then PA * PB = PC * PD (where PA is the whole secant, PB is the external part).
• Tangent-Secant: If PT is a tangent and PAB is a secant, then PT^2 = PA * PB.
This value (d^2 - R^2) is constant for any specific point relative to a circle.
In a cyclic quadrilateral ABCD, angle A = 70° and angle ABD = 40°. What is the measure of angle ACD?

Solution: This is a classic angle chasing problem using arcs. 
Angle ABD is an inscribed angle that intercepts arc AD. So, arc AD is 2 * 40° = 80°. 
Now look at angle ACD. It is also an inscribed angle, and it intercepts the EXACT SAME arc AD! 
Therefore, angle ACD must be equal to angle ABD. Angle ACD = 40°. 
(Note: Angle A = 70° was extra information meant to test your confidence in the inscribed angle theorem!).
Olympiad Problem 2: Power of a Point
From an external point P, a tangent PT and a secant PAB are drawn to a circle. If the external part of the secant PB = 4 and the internal chord BA = 5, what is the length of the tangent PT?

Solution: We use the Tangent-Secant version of the Power of a Point theorem: PT^2 = PA * PB. 
Be very careful here: PA is the ENTIRE length of the secant, not just the inside chord. 
PA = PB + BA = 4 + 5 = 9. 
Now apply the formula: PT^2 = 9 * 4 = 36. 
Taking the square root, PT = 6. The length of the tangent is 6.
